issues.description: The template's UniqueTable constructor requires a parameter (size: int) but the module then creates the global unique-table instance with no argument (UT = UniqueTable()). This is an internal contradiction in template_repository/dd.py that will raise a TypeError on import (missing required positional argument) and thus prevents students from running or testing the template. The solution implementation uses a no-argument constructor for UniqueTable, so the intended design is a parameterless __init__ — the template should match that.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template UniqueTable constructor signature match the intended (and solution) no-argument form. Concretely, change def __init__(self, size: int) -> None: to def __init__(self) -> None: (and remove or handle any use of self.size), or alternatively instantiate UT with a concrete size (e.g. UT = UniqueTable(<size>)). The simplest fix to preserve the exercise flow is to adopt the no-argument constructor (as in the solution) so UT = UniqueTable() works.
